t: What Makes a Good Build Request
name: What Makes a Good Build Request
title: What Makes a Good Build Request
description: Good requests state the goal, constraints, and context: what to build, for whom, with what limits. 'Build a shelf' is weak; 'build a 4-foot oak bookshelf for paperbacks, under $80, with hand tools' is plannable.
how_it_works: Include goal, key dimensions, materials preference, budget, tools available, timeline, and skill level. The more concrete the request, the less the plan must assume.
key_points: Goal, dimensions, materials, budget, tools, timeline, skill.
Context (who, where, why) shapes the plan.
Vague in, vague out: specify to get specificity.
requirements: A natural-language build request; a defined output plan format; constraint inputs (budget, tools, timeline, skills).
standards: Work-breakdown and planning practice; prompt/result documentation standards.
citations: Project planning literature (work breakdown structures, critical path).
Human-computer interaction guidance on natural-language interfaces.

name: Parsing Intent from Description
title: Parsing Intent from Description
description: Parsing extracts the buildable facts from prose: the object, its key attributes, constraints, and priorities. It separates what was said from what was meant.
how_it_works: Read the request listing facts (dimensions, materials, quantities), constraints (budget, tools, time), and priorities (what matters most). Flag ambiguities explicitly rather than resolving them silently.
key_points: Extract facts, constraints, priorities from prose.
Separate what was said from what was meant.
The parsed fact list is the plan's foundation.

name: Scope: What's In and Out
title: Scope: What's In and Out
description: Scope defines the plan's boundaries: included work, excluded work, and assumptions. Unscoped plans grow without limit; scoped plans can be judged complete.
how_it_works: Write explicit in-scope and out-of-scope lists from the request, and confirm them before planning. Changes to scope re-plan; scope creep without re-planning is how budgets die.
requirements: A natural-language build request; a defined output plan format; constraint inputs (budget, tools, timeline, skills).

name: From Request to Step List
title: From Request to Step List
description: The core conversion: a described goal becomes an ordered list of steps. Each step needs its action, materials, tools, and a way to know it's done right.
how_it_works: Break the goal into major phases, then steps within phases, ordering by dependency. For each step record: do-what, with-what, check-how. Review the list for missing steps by walking it mentally.
key_points: Phases, then steps, ordered by dependency.
Each step: action, materials, tools, check.
The step list is the plan's backbone.
requirements: A natural-language build request; a defined output plan format; constraint inputs (budget, tools, timeline, skills).

name: Materials Lists from Descriptions
title: Materials Lists from Descriptions
description: Descriptions imply materials ('oak bookshelf' implies oak boards); the plan makes them explicit with sizes, quantities, and allowances. Implied is not specified.
how_it_works: Convert material mentions to line items with dimensions, quantities, grades, and waste allowance. Where the request is silent, propose options with trade-offs rather than assuming.
key_points: Implied materials made explicit: size, quantity, grade.
Silence gets options with trade-offs, not assumptions.
The materials list is purchasable or it's not done.

key_points: Every step mapped to its tools.

Check against available tools before starting.

name: Time Estimates from Plans
title: Time Estimates from Plans
description: Time estimates come from the step list: each step's duration estimated, summed with contingency. Estimates without steps are guesses; with steps they are calculations.
how_it_works: Estimate per step (using experience or references), sum them, and add contingency (20-50% for unfamiliar work). Present as a range, and track actuals to improve future estimates.
key_points: Estimate per step, sum with contingency.
Track actuals to calibrate future estimates.
Steps make estimates calculations, not guesses.
requirements: A natural-language build request; a defined output plan format; constraint inputs (budget, tools, timeline, skills).
standards: Work-breakdown and planning practice; prompt/result documentation standards.

name: Constraint Checking
title: Constraint Checking
description: Plans must be checked against the request's constraints: budget, tools, timeline, skill. A plan violating its constraints is a pretty failure.
how_it_works: Cost the materials list, sum the time estimate, verify tool availability, and assess skill demands against the builder. Where constraints break, offer scoped alternatives - smaller, simpler, or phased.
key_points: Cost, time, tools, skill checked against constraints.
Violations get scoped alternatives, not hope.
Constraints are the plan's reality check.
requirements: A natural-language build request; a defined output plan format; constraint inputs (budget, tools, timeline, skills).
standards: Work-breakdown and planning practice; prompt/result documentation standards.

name: Skill-Level Adaptation
title: Skill-Level Adaptation
description: The same goal needs different plans for beginners and experts: more detail, safer methods, and simpler joints for beginners; efficiency for experts. One plan does not fit all skills.
how_it_works: Assess the builder's skill from the request (or ask), then adapt: detailed steps and safety notes for beginners, streamlined for experts. Never assign expert-only techniques to beginners silently.
key_points: Adapt detail and method to stated skill.
Beginners get detail, safety notes, simple methods.
Ask skill level when the request doesn't say.
requirements: A natural-language build request; a defined output plan format; constraint inputs (budget, tools, timeline, skills).

name: Verification Steps in Plans
title: Verification Steps in Plans

key_points: Specify what to verify and to what tolerance.

Quality is planned, not inspected in later.
